title: Comparison of methods for plasma protein binding of anti-infectives using NMR and HPLC
summary: When antibiotics circulate in the blood, only the part that is not bound to proteins can actually fight infections. Measuring this “free” part is difficult. Usually, laboratories use a process called ultrafiltration before measuring the concentration with a standard chemical test (HPLC). This study explores whether a newer technique, called quantitative NMR (qNMR), can directly measure the free part of the antibiotic piperacillin without such extra steps. The researchers will compare both methods using leftover blood samples from routine testing. The goal is to see if qNMR could be a simpler and reliable alternative, not to test how well the drug works.

interventions.name: A method comparison between qNMR and HPLC is performed using residual material samples from routine tests to investigate the feasibility of measuring the free concentration of piperacillin directly using qNMR. HPLC after ultrafiltration is used for comparison.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
ICU stay
Piperacillin therapy
Routine blood draws with residuals available
